newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: BAESA mulls sale of Chilean unit.
newsitem.headline: BAESA mulls sale of Chilean unit.

text.p: Buenos Aires Embotelladora SA (BAESA), Pepsi Co's biggest bottler outside the United States, is mulling the sale of its Chilean interests, President and CEO Luis Suarez said Friday.
"We are considering a possible spin-off of our stake in bottling company ECUSA in Chile," he told Reuters.
"But we may not be able to do that as new investors may want to keep that company. It is highly profitable."
ECUSA is a joint venture between BAESA, which owns 45 percent, and brewer Companias Cervecerias Unidas SA, which holds 55 percent.
"In Brazil and Argentina we are exploring alliances, capitalization alternatives, focusing first on Brazil."
Suarez said he was taken totally by surprise by a steep fall of BAESA's ADRs, which declined nearly 40 percent from Thursday. "The fall was a real surprise. I don't understand it all."
He added he was not aware of any new development.
Earlier this month, BAESA said it failed to pay about $500 million in obligations due March 31 under a standstill agreement.

Suarez said that when that agreement expired, the company could have renewed it for a short while, but decided to wait for a "clearer restructuring and that takes time. I am upbeat about negotiations."

He added the company was exploring alternatives, including debt-for-equity swaps with creditor banks and a capital injection, but he dismissed any possibility of taking shares out of circulation and reiterated that BAESA has no plans to file for bankruptcy protection against creditors.
Suarez also said BAESA was actively negotiating with Pepsi -- which took over managing the bottler last July -- in search of additional support for the bottler's revamping.
BAESA is undergoing a financial crunch widely blamed on overexpansion. In 1996, BAESA lost $452.4 million, after turning a $44.8 million profit in 1995.

BAESA has the exclusive Pepsi and Seven-Up franchises for the Buenos Aires metropolitan area and other regions in Argentina, as well as Chile, Uruguay and Costa Rica and certain Southern Brazilian states, including the metropolitan areas of Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro.
